title: The Left-Right Flip
description: Umbra scrawls a secret word that only reads correctly in a mirror. Crack lateral inversion to read his plan and grab the shard.

content.value: Why Your Right Hand Looks Like a Left Hand
In a plane mirror, left and right appear swapped. This left-to-right flip is called LATERAL INVERSION. Raise your right hand and your mirror image raises what looks like its left hand.
The word AMBULANCE is often written reversed on the front of the vehicle. Why? So a driver ahead sees it the RIGHT way round in their rear-view mirror and quickly moves aside.

Written on ambulance:   ƎƆNA˩UᗺMA
Seen in your mirror:    AMBULANCE   ✅ readable!

Some capital letters look the SAME in a mirror because they are symmetrical left-to-right: A, H, I, M, O, T, U, V, W, X, Y. Letters like B, P, R, S and words like 'LIGHT' get flipped and look reversed.
Top and bottom are NOT swapped in a plane mirror — only left and right. Your image is still the right way up, just laterally inverted.
Key Takeaway: Lateral inversion is the left-right swap seen in a plane mirror. It flips most letters and words, which is why 'AMBULANCE' is written reversed on rescue vehicles.

quiz.question: Lateral inversion means a plane mirror swaps…
quiz.explain: A plane mirror flips left and right (lateral inversion). Top and bottom stay the same.

quiz.question: Why is 'AMBULANCE' written reversed on the front of the vehicle?
options: So drivers ahead read it correctly in their rear-view mirror
quiz.explain: The rear-view mirror laterally inverts the reversed word back to normal, so drivers ahead can read 'AMBULANCE' instantly.

quiz.question: Which capital letter looks the SAME in a plane mirror?
quiz.explain: 'A' is symmetrical left-to-right, so it is unchanged. 'R' and 'B' look reversed.
